mode: VERIFICATION (Thompson 1917 claim override) — not a new-model scout

claim.citation: Thompson, D.W. (1917) On Growth and Form. Cambridge University Press. Ch. XII 'The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera', pp. 587-611, Figs. 308-317.
claim.text: Foraminiferal shells are generated by chambers added in logarithmic-spiral succession with (near-)constant growth ratios, and the genera form a continuous geometric series transformable into one another.
thompsons_own_quantitative_evidence: p. 593: von Moller (1878) Fusulina cylindrica whorl breadths I-IV = 0.132, 0.195, 0.300, 0.449 mm; F. boecki I-V = 0.079, 0.120, 0.180, 0.264, 0.396 mm; 'very nearly in the ratio of 1 : 1.5'.

p. 593: von Moller F. cylindrica opposite (180-degree-apart) whorls 0.096 ... 0.395 mm; mean log10 difference 0.088 = log 1.225 per half-whorl, 0.176 = log 1.5 per whorl; constant angle about 86 degrees.
p. 595: van Iterson (1907) Triloculina rotunda chambers 2-10 breadth 34 ... 319 um, mean ratio 1.323 = (319/34)^(1/8).
p. 595: Rhumbler, Pulvinulina menardii mean linear chamber ratio about 1.187, 'not strictly constant from chamber to chamber, but subject to a small secondary fluctuation'.
p. 597-598: constant ratio of chamber volumes V_{n+1}/V_n = 1 + q derived from growth proportional to existing mass; similar chambers subtending equal angles => logarithmic spiral.

p. 602-605: the genera (rotaline spirals, Miliolidae at 180/120 degrees, Nodosarian straight limit, Textularian helicoid, Orbitolitid circular limit with constant angle 90 degrees) 'all come under the head of the logarithmic spiral' and 'any one must tend to pass into any other by small and continuous gradations'.

dataset.title: Data from: Heterochronic origin of spherical fusulinid foraminifera in the Late Paleozoic
dataset.download_url_used: https://datadryad.org/api/v2/versions/84334/download (public zip; per-file API downloads require a bearer token)
dataset.content: 1396 axial-thin-section test outlines (4 landmarks + 36 semilandmarks = 40 (x, y) pixel coordinates each) for 106 fusulinid specimens: Triticites (40; Gzhelian + Asselian-Sakmarian), Pseudoschwagerina (15), Sphaeroschwagerina (13), Zellia (13), Robustoschwagerina (25). Each outline 'NAME-k' / 'k-NAME' is the test outline at whorl-growing stage k; successive stages alternate centroid side, i.e. they are HALF-whorl (180 degree) stages — exactly the 'opposite whorls, 180 degrees apart' series von Moller measured and Thompson tabulated on p. 593.

why_it_matches: TAXON: Thompson's only tabulated whorl-ratio data for the claim are von Moller's Fusulina (Carboniferous fusulinid foraminifera). The Dryad data are fusulinid foraminifera (Triticites and four pseudoschwagerine genera, Gzhelian-Sakmarian), i.e. the same superfamily as Thompson's exemplar; Triticites is a direct triticitid relative of von Moller's Fusulina s.l.

VARIABLE: Thompson's test statistic is the ratio of breadths of successive (half-)whorls along one radius in the coiling plane. From each stage outline we recover the test diameter perpendicular to the coiling axis (and the axial length), giving the successive-whorl size series D_1 ... D_K per specimen with K = 10-18 half-whorl stages.

CLAIM PART 2: five genera spanning the fusiform -> spherical transition allow the 'continuous geometric series / transformable into one another' part to be tested as a continuum of per-specimen growth ratio and length/diameter allometry across genera.
limitations: Whorl-level (as in von Moller), not chamber-level: septal chambers within a whorl are not digitized. The chamber-level ratio part (van Iterson Triloculina 1.323; Rhumbler Pulvinulina 1.187) is tested only against Thompson's own published series and against the Fig. 309 Nummulina section via computer vision.
Pixel coordinates without a scale bar: all tests are scale-free (ratios, log-slopes).

Late Paleozoic fusulinids only; Thompson's Figs. 308-317 genera (Hastigerina, Nummulina, Cornuspira, Operculina, Miliolina, Cyclammina, Orbulina, Cristellaria, Discorbina, Textularia) are represented only by the Fig. 309 Nummulina section and by the generative model, not by modern measured specimens.
dataset_verification.verdict_on_mismatch_rule: Not a DATASET_MISMATCH: variables and taxon class match Thompson's own exemplar (Fusulina). Pseudoschwagerine genera are an in-scope extension (same superfamily, same measurement), not an analogue.

planned_tests: T1: per-specimen log-linear fit log D_k = a + k log rho (geometric / logarithmic-spiral succession) — r, RMSE, and comparison against arithmetic (linear) and quadratic-in-log (drifting ratio) alternatives by BIC.
T2: constancy of successive half-whorl ratios: CV of D_{k+1}/D_k per specimen; trend test of ratio vs stage (Thompson's 'small secondary fluctuation' vs systematic ontogenetic drift).
T3: Triticites whorl ratio vs von Moller/Thompson 1.225 per half-whorl (1.5 per whorl).
T4: continuity of the genus series: distribution of per-specimen rho and length/diameter allometry across five genera — overlap, gaps, nearest-neighbour statistics.
T5: CV extraction of whorl-wall radii from Thompson Fig. 309 (Nummulina) along radial rays; fit r(theta) = a e^{b theta}; compare successive whorl ratio.

T6: generative model (chambers at constant angle increment, constant linear ratio) reproduces Thompson's series of genera (Globigerina-like, Cyclammina 20-degree, Miliolid 180/120-degree, Nodosarian limit, Orbitolitid limit) with continuous interpolation.
